entity.name: Garrett Elliott
entity.description: Independent developer building free reading and study tools, published at breadtoasting.com. The work centres on people who find ordinary text hard to read — dyslexic readers, low-vision readers, readers with visual stress or attention difficulties — and on keeping those tools free, offline, and free of tracking so they can be used by schools, libraries, and anyone else without a procurement conversation or a privacy trade-off. Everything is MIT-licensed and developed in the open.

projects.name: Reader Comfort
projects.description:
A cross-browser extension (Chrome, Edge, Firefox) that applies a full set of reading aids to any web page: page tint, text size, line and letter spacing, accessible typefaces (Atkinson Hyperlegible, Lexend, OpenDyslexic — all bundled, none fetched), a narrow reading measure, and a pointer-following reading ruler. It also carries a persistent highlighter, a freehand annotation layer, sticky notes, and a bundled PDF.js viewer with a reflowing reading mode, because a fixed PDF layout is otherwise closed to every one of these aids.

It collects nothing. No account, no server, no analytics. Settings live in the browser's own storage; highlights, notes and ink stay on the device. The single optional network call is a dictionary lookup that is off by default and sends one word. That posture is deliberate: it is what makes the extension safe to place in front of schoolchildren without a data-sharing agreement.

The interface passes its own WCAG 2.2 A/AA audit with zero violations, verified with axe-core against the built package rather than asserted. Recent work added a shortcut and macro editor, so any reading action can be bound to a key of the reader's choosing. Administrator policy support — so a school can push a configuration to managed devices rather than ask every reader to set it up by hand — is in progress and is the next release.

plans.name: Reader Comfort — a year of maintenance and school deployment
plans.description: A year of full-time-equivalent maintenance on Reader Comfort: keeping the extension current with Chrome and Firefox extension platform changes, completing administrator-policy deployment so schools and libraries can roll it out across managed devices, publishing an accessibility conformance report for public-sector procurement, translating the interface, and supporting pilot deployments. The aim is that a school can adopt it without buying anything and without signing anything away.
